summary: American airline executive Frank Lorenzo took over Texas International, Continental and Eastern from the 1970s, using strikes, scab labor and a 1983 bankruptcy to break airline unions and cut pay, until his empire collapsed in 1990.

evidence.note: Lorenzo's birth in New York City in 1940 opens the biography
elected president and CEO of Texas International in August 1972, start of main span
ground workers strike at Texas International from December 1974 and his refusal to concede
extended segment on corporate raiders and private equity as his peer group
Continental unions and CEO Feldman try an employee buyout to block the takeover
Feldman's suicide after the buyout financing collapses in 1981
plan to use Chapter 11 bankruptcy to void union contracts at Continental
1989 Eastern machinists strike, sympathy strikes, collapse and ban from the airline industry

notes: Lorenzo was alive at release, so the lifetime rule sets covered_span end to 2023. Early aviation history (Robert Six, Rickenbacker, CAB regulation) is background and does not extend covered_span. No theme for deregulation or transport policy; finance-crypto stands in for corporate raiding. Feldman's birth year is not given; the transcript only says he was 53.
